trust_decision.summary: install -D decides 'the destination parent already exists' by following symlinks and then creates leading directories with fs::create_dir_all and writes the destination with a path-based remove_file + create_new, so a pre-existing symlink anywhere in DEST's leading path redirects the write.

landing_point.why: This is the only leading-directory creation in the -D path (fs::create_dir_all(to_create)) and it follows a pre-existing symlink component; an engineer reading the advisory summary looks here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: install -D SRC DEST (create-leading branch of standard())
install (all modes; path-based copy_file kept as the second implementation)
install (copy() split so finalize_installed_file is shared)
public library API uucore::safe_traversal::DirFd, re-exported at src/uucore/src/lib/lib.rs:103 and used by install, chmod, du, rm and chown

O3_reason_to_dismiss: safe_traversal is shared chmod/du/rm/chown traversal plumbing, not the install code the report names, and its callers rely on DirFd::open following symlinks, so an install -D advisory need not change that library API.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: chmod -R and chown -R must keep following a symlinked directory given on the command line (TraverseSymlinks::First/All) instead of replacing it; making DirFd::open no-follow by default breaks that.

O6_input_shapes: DEST whose leading directories do not exist (created by -D)
DEST whose parent already exists as a real directory (fd opened with NoFollow)
pre-existing symlink as the deepest existing path component (unlinked and replaced with a real directory)
pre-existing symlink at the final destination component (unlink_at before open_file_at)
path component that exists but is not a directory (NotADirectory error)
multiple sources copied into a directory
destination that exists as a regular file versus a new path
source and destination that are the same inode (dev/ino check via stat_at)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: install -d DIR creates directory components with fs::create_dir_all, which follows a pre-existing symlink component and creates the remaining directories inside the link target; the published fix left directory() untouched.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: install -d is mkdir-like, has no destination file to overwrite, and the advisory names -D, so the route was never covered and is arguably a different feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, separate MainFunction::Directory entry point about 15 lines above the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: install -D SRC DEST where DEST is a pre-existing symlink to a directory: is_potential_directory_path() follows the link (path.is_dir()), so the copy goes through copy_files_into_dir/copy_file and the file is written inside the link target instead of the link being replaced.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: DEST names an existing directory, so install is copying into it rather than creating -D leading directories; following a destination directory the user named is documented install behaviour, and the fix explicitly excludes is_potential_directory_path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, copy_files_into_dir at src/uu/install/src/install.rs:699 and copy_file at src/uu/install/src/install.rs:815

O8_uncovered_routes.route: install -D -t DIR SRC (and -t with several sources): create_dir_all_safe's DirFd, and in the pinned code the path-based creation, is not carried to the copy because target_parent_fd is only kept when target_dir.is_none(), so the final write still goes through path-based copy_file.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the -t route's directory creation is already made safe by the fix, so the remaining exposure is only a concurrent swap of DIR after creation, not the static pre-existing-symlink case in the report.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, copy_files_into_dir path at src/uu/install/src/install.rs:699-723

O8b_injection_room.sibling: make install -d use create_dir_all_safe as well
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: directory() is the other fs::create_dir_all caller in the same file, so a maintainer closing the -D race would naturally unify directory creation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: anchor the copy_files_into_dir branch to the DirFd returned by create_dir_all_safe
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix already produces that fd for target-directory mode and then drops it, so keeping it for the copy is a small, natural follow-up.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: give copy_file an O_NOFOLLOW/openat-based write so non--D routes are covered too
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: copy_file is the path-based second implementation the fix left in place, and its own comment claims create_new is TOCTOU protection.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: extend DirFd::open/open_subdir with a no-follow behaviour instead of a plain path open
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the shared traversal helper is the primitive install uses for the fix, and it is already shared by chmod, du, rm and chown.

O10_build.project_tests: tests/by-util/test_install.rs, gated by the `install` feature at tests/tests.rs:191-193; run with `cargo test --features install --test tests test_install`

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: check !path.is_symlink() or canonicalize the parent before fs::create_dir_all in standard() and keep the path-based copy_file, leaving install -d, the -t copy and the race windows open.

out_of_scope_notes: uu_mkdir, uu_cp and uu_mv have their own path-based directory creation (src/uu/mkdir/src/mkdir.rs:288, src/uu/cp/src/copydir.rs:612, src/uu/mv/src/mv.rs:1007); those are different commands' protected operations, not this install -D advisory, and were not pursued.

After the safe copy, install still finalizes through the path (mode::chmod at src/uu/install/src/mode.rs:17, plus chown/strip/timestamps); that is a metadata sink, not the arbitrary-file-overwrite sink, and was not pursued.
